narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To show how US music sales in 2015 split across digital, physical, and other formats.

units.meaning: In the United States, digital accounted for 66% of music sales.
accepted_routes: 66% of US music sales were digital.
Roughly two-thirds of US music sales were digital.
units.visual_evidence_rule: A label or slice for Digital must show 66% in the US/overall donut.
units.temporal_anchor: first narration clause: '66% of US music sales were digital'
units.reviewer_question: Must the clip explicitly state the US digital share as 66%?

units.meaning: In the United States, physical accounted for 19% of music sales.
accepted_routes: 19% of US music sales were physical.
Physical media was under one-fifth of US music sales.
units.visual_evidence_rule: A label or slice for Physical must show 19% in the US/overall donut.
units.temporal_anchor: first narration clause / complement of the 66% digital statement
units.reviewer_question: Must the clip explicitly state the US physical share as 19%?

optional_valid: Digital was the majority format in the US because its share is above 50%.
The year 2015 is valid as the clip's stated time context.
US digital share was roughly two-thirds of sales.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claims about why digital displaced physical.
Extrapolation to other years or countries not present in the table.
Adding streaming, vinyl, CD, or other format categories not in the table.
Treating revenue shares and unit shares as interchangeable or using a wrong denominator.
notes: The table supports the US composition Digital 66% + Physical 19% + other 15% = 100%.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
